name: Search-o1: Agentic Search-Enhanced Large Reasoning Models
authors_affiliation: Xiaoxi Li, Guanting Dong, Jiajie Jin, Yuyao Zhang, Yutao Zhu, Peitian Zhang, Zhicheng Dou (Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence, Renmin University of China); Yujia Zhou (Tsinghua University). Corresponding author: Zhicheng Dou (RUC).
code_url: https://github.com/RUC-NLPIR/Search-o1 (originally referenced as https://github.com/sunnynexus/Search-o1 in v1 abstract). Project page: https://search-o1.github.io/
task_domain: Complex multi-step reasoning (PhD-level science QA, mathematics, code generation) plus open-domain QA (single-hop and multi-hop). Augments o1-style large reasoning models (LRMs) with on-demand web retrieval.
problem_setting: Inference-time / test-time framework (no training of the backbone LRM). A single LRM (QwQ-32B-Preview) reasons autonomously and, when it hits a knowledge gap during its long chain-of-thought, emits a search query, retrieves documents from a live web search engine, refines them, and continues reasoning. Single-agent (one reasoning model that also doubles as the Reason-in-Documents refiner via a separate generation pass). No fine-tuning or supervision; the backbone is frozen and used in a prompting/inference-only manner. Supports batch inference over multiple questions in parallel.
what_is_retrieved: External web documents/pages (open-web knowledge) retrieved on demand to fill knowledge gaps in the reasoning chain.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus (the open web via Bing Web Search API; Wikipedia-backed corpora for open-domain QA benchmarks). No agent-written/episodic memory; retrieval targets a fixed external knowledge source.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective (top-10 documents per search query, configurable k); the system issues multiple retrievals across reasoning steps to incrementally cover the diverse knowledge needs, but each retrieval is a fixed top-k call rather than a completeness-driven variable-size set.
retrieval_unit: document / web page (top-k retrieved documents per query; in the RAgent baseline top-10 snippets first, then full documents fetched by URL via Jina Reader API). After refinement the injected unit is a distilled text passage.
index_source: Static external store: live web index queried through the Bing Web Search API (and Wikipedia-based corpora for open-domain QA). Not offline-induced and not grown by the agent at test time.
index_structure_topology: Flat external search index (commercial web search engine inverted index / Wikipedia dense or sparse index). No graph or hierarchical structure imposed by the method.
retriever_type: Off-the-shelf web search engine (Bing Web Search API) as the retriever; for open-domain QA benchmarks a standard retriever over Wikipedia is used. Effectively BM25/dense-style search engine, not learned by the method.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The retriever is not trained or fine-tuned; the LRM only learns nothing here either (frozen). Retrieval quality depends on the underlying search engine.
query_construction: Thought-conditioned: the LRM autonomously generates a targeted natural-language search query (e.g., 'structure of trans-Cinnamaldehyde') based on the current reasoning state and previously retrieved knowledge, emitted between special symbols <|begin_search_query|> and <|end_search_query|>.
query_granularity: Step/state-level: queries are generated at the reasoning step where the model encounters uncertainty (mid-chain), not a single task-level query at t=0. Multiple queries can be issued within one reasoning session.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative and agent-initiated (agentic / active): the model decides when to retrieve, triggering retrieval whenever it emits a search-query special token; can iterate multiple times within a single reasoning chain.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent-initiated request via generated special tokens. When the model decodes the <|end_search_query|> symbol, generation is paused and the enclosed query triggers retrieval. The trigger is the model's own decision (driven by knowledge uncertainty during reasoning, motivated by high frequency of uncertain words like 'perhaps'), not a fixed schedule, external confidence threshold, or trained classifier.
reranking: No dedicated reranking stage described. The search engine returns top-k; the Reason-in-Documents module performs analysis/extraction rather than learned reranking.
retrieved_context_refinement: Reason-in-Documents distillation: a separate generation pass (using the same reasoning model) analyzes the top-k retrieved documents conditioned on the current search query and prior reasoning steps, producing a concise 'Final Information' refined snippet (or 'No helpful information found.'). This minimizes noise/redundancy and preserves coherence before injection. Two-stage: intermediate analysis reasoning r_docs then refined output r_final.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the refined knowledge r_final is injected back into the ongoing reasoning chain between special symbols <|begin_search_result|> and <|end_search_result|>, and the LRM continues reasoning. Not used as a training signal.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved inside the reasoning/search loop: the reasoning chain is paused at the point a search query is emitted, retrieval + Reason-in-Documents refinement runs, the refined result is inserted, and reasoning resumes. This is a retrieve-within-reasoning loop (agentic RAG) rather than plan-then-retrieve or tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-CoT-step / per-search-step within a single rollout: retrieval is woven in at each point where the model decodes a search-query special token during its long reasoning chain (can be multiple times per question).
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled free-text knowledge (the 'Final Information' refined passage produced by the Reason-in-Documents module), injected as text between search-result special tokens. Raw documents are not injected directly in Search-o1 (they are in the RAgent baseline).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled, query-and-context-conditioned factual snippet derived from raw web documents (an extracted/condensed insight rather than a raw trajectory or a single demonstration).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Reason-in-Documents refinement module: it filters redundant/irrelevant content from verbose retrieved documents and outputs only concise relevant information (or explicitly 'No helpful information found.'), guarding the main reasoning chain against noise and incoherence introduced by directly inserting long documents. No retriever-aware training or distractor-aware SFT (inference-only).
memory_type: none (no persistent episodic/skill/workflow memory). The framework is stateless across questions; retrieved knowledge lives only within the current reasoning session.
write_back: No. The system does not store new experiences/cases/skills into any memory for later retrieval; refined knowledge is used only in-context for the current question.
online_growth: No. The retrievable store (web search index) is external and not grown by the agent at deployment/test time.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back to a memory store).
failure_experience_usage: N/A — no experience storage. Failed or successful reasoning trajectories are not retained or retrieved; there is no success/failure memory.
memory_evolution_update: N/A — no stored memory entries to mutate (no append/merge/refine/prune).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/when-to-search is an emergent prompting behavior of the frozen LRM via special tokens, not an RL-optimized or learned retrieval policy. (Search-o1 is inference-only; trained-policy successors such as Search-R1 came later.)
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private reasoning; no memory or experience shared across agents or frameworks. (Batch inference processes multiple independent questions in parallel but they do not share knowledge.)
benchmarks: Challenging reasoning: GPQA (diamond 198 / extended 546, PhD-level science MCQA in physics/chemistry/biology), MATH500, AMC2023 (40 q), AIME2024 (30 q), LiveCodeBench (112 problems, Aug-Nov 2024). Open-domain QA: Natural Questions (NQ), TriviaQA (single-hop); HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA (2WIKI), MuSiQue, Bamboogle (multi-hop).
benchmark_family: QA (GPQA science MCQA; NQ, TriviaQA single-hop), multi-hop (HotpotQA, 2WIKI, MuSiQue, Bamboogle), math (MATH500, AMC2023, AIME2024), code (LiveCodeBench).
baselines: Direct Reasoning w/o retrieval: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, QwQ-32B-Preview, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, Llama3.3-70B-Instruct, and (reference) DeepSeek-R1-Lite-Preview, GPT-4o, o1-preview. Retrieval-augmented: Standard RAG (top-10 docs for the original question, RAG-Qwen2.5-32B / RAG-QwQ-32B) and RAG Agent (RAgent, ReAct-style top-10 snippets then URL fetch, RAgent-Qwen2.5-32B / RAgent-QwQ-32B). Also human experts on GPQA extended set.
key_metrics: Pass@1 (reported for all challenging reasoning tasks: GPQA, math, LiveCodeBench). Exact Match (EM) and F1 for open-domain QA. GPQA also broken down by Physics/Chemistry/Biology and Overall.
headline_result: On the GPQA diamond set Search-o1 (QwQ-32B-Preview backbone) reaches 63.6 overall Pass@1, exceeding RAgent-QwQ-32B (61.6) and direct QwQ-32B (58.1); on the GPQA extended set it surpasses human experts overall (57.9). Averaged across the five challenging reasoning datasets, Search-o1 exceeds RAgent-QwQ-32B by 4.7%, QwQ-32B by 3.1%, and non-reasoning Qwen2.5-32B / Llama3.3-70B by 44.7% / 39.3%.
ablations: Reason-in-Documents ablation: Search-o1 vs RAgent-QwQ-32B (agentic RAG that injects raw documents) isolates the Reason-in-Documents refinement (+4.7% avg on reasoning tasks; +5.3% avg EM on multi-hop QA). Agentic-RAG vs Standard-RAG ablation: agentic RAG (RAgent) gives +23.2% avg EM over standard RAG on multi-hop QA for QwQ-32B, while single-hop QA shows little change (47.8 vs 47.6 EM). Scaling analysis on number of retrieved documents (top-k): retrieving even one document with Search-o1 surpasses Direct Reasoning and standard RAG using ten documents. Non-reasoning model (Qwen2.5-32B) with agentic RAG performs no better or worse than standard RAG, showing ordinary LLMs cannot effectively use search as a tool.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (Pass@1, EM, F1) are reported; intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval completeness) are not reported separately.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (final-answer Pass@1 / EM / F1). Process quality is illustrated qualitatively via case studies (Appendix B on GPQA, AMC2023, HotpotQA) showing coherent interleaving of search queries and refined results, and via a preliminary analysis counting uncertain words ('perhaps', etc.) in reasoning chains, but no quantitative step-wise process score.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discusses efficiency via a batch inference mechanism that parallelizes both token generation and Reason-in-Documents refinement across multiple questions to improve throughput. Scaling analysis shows Search-o1 with a single retrieved document can beat baselines using ten documents (more cost-effective use of retrieval). Hardware: eight NVIDIA A800-80GB GPUs. No explicit per-question API-cost or latency numbers reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k retrieval: top-k = 10 documents per search query by default (Bing region US-EN), with a scaling analysis over k. Generation budget: up to 32,768 max tokens, temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, repetition penalty 1.05. Reason-in-Documents compresses the top-k documents into a short refined snippet before injection, capping injected context.
builds_on: Large reasoning models (OpenAI-o1, Qwen QwQ-32B-Preview as backbone, DeepSeek-R1); agentic RAG / ReAct-style tool-use; chain-of-thought prompting; retrieval-augmented generation. Uses Bing Web Search API and Jina Reader API.
contrasts_with: Standard (one-shot, problem-oriented) RAG that retrieves once and injects raw top-k documents; plain agentic RAG / RAgent (ReAct-style) that injects lengthy raw retrieved documents and disrupts reasoning coherence; direct reasoning without retrieval (knowledge-insufficient); MCTS-based o1 reproductions that rely on external policy/reward models without internalized reasoning.
lineage: Group B (retrieval-augmented task solving / agentic RAG for reasoning). An inference-time agentic-RAG-for-reasoning framework that bridges o1-style LRMs with on-demand web retrieval plus document distillation; a direct precursor to later RL-trained search-augmented reasoning models (e.g., Search-R1, R1-Searcher, ReSearch) that train the search policy rather than prompt it.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A — not a case-based reasoning method. Implements only a Retrieve-like step (web retrieval); no Reuse/Revise/Retain of cases.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is positioned as agentic RAG for large reasoning models.
tool_document_engineering: N/A — Search-o1 retrieves web documents, not tools/APIs; no tool-description engineering. (The Reason-in-Documents module post-processes retrieved documents but this is query-time refinement, not pre-indexing tool-document engineering.)
index_content_separation: Partial/related: in the RAgent baseline, lightweight top-10 snippets are retrieved first and full documents are fetched by URL on demand (progressive disclosure). Search-o1 itself relies on the Reason-in-Documents module to condense full retrieved content rather than a separate lightweight index.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A — no tool index. Retrieval uses the live Bing Web Search API and Jina Reader API for page content; integration is via API calls within the inference loop (not MCP/RapidAPI tool registries).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A — no inter-tool dependency modeling (the only external tool is web search).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A — not CBR; no retrieved-case adaptation/revision. (The closest analog is the Reason-in-Documents distillation that adapts raw documents into context-fit refined knowledge.)
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A — this is a method paper, not a survey/taxonomy.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A — uses existing benchmarks (does not construct a new benchmark). Sizes of evaluation sets noted: GPQA diamond 198 / extended 546; MATH500 500; AMC2023 40; AIME2024 30; LiveCodeBench 112 (Aug-Nov 2024).
